name: gateway-client.md
text:
# Talking to the gateway

Agents send every gateway request through `com.blockether.vis.internal.gateway.client`.
Its `request!` function finds or starts the daemon, takes a lease and adds authentication.
A 4xx or 5xx response is data, so the session code checks the status itself.

The wire format lives in com.blockether.vis.contract.wire: call `->wire` before
`json-str` so every key is snake_case. See [[Gateway lease model]] for the lease rules
and the Gateway client concept for the ownership model.

The server side is com.blockether.vis.internal.gateway.server and it keeps per-session
data in com.blockether.vis.internal.gateway.state. Push delivery goes through
src/com/blockether/vis/internal/gateway/relay.clj when a relay grant exists.

name: companion-sync.md
text:
## Companion live sync

The Companion app opens one `GatewayClient` (see apps/vis-companion/src/lib/gateway.ts)
and hands it to SessionSubscriptionHub, which keeps a cursor per session and replays
missed events after a reconnect.

On iOS and Android the sign-in flow uses the native OAuthLoopback plugin. Its
`.callback()` method receives the redirect. The Python SDK has a different
GatewayClient in packages/vis-agent/src/blockether/vis/engine/_client.py; the app never
loads it.

Status: done. Changed: the hub now drops a stale story when the user changes the
session list. Fixed the meta row.

name: sandbox-policy.md
text:
# Sandbox policy review

The host policy is in com.blockether.vis.internal.sandbox.policy and the scoped rules in
com.blockether.vis.internal.sandbox.scoped-policy. The jail itself is
`com.blockether.vis.internal.sandbox.jail`; its tests are in
com.blockether.vis.internal.sandbox.jail-test.

Network egress runs through com.blockether.vis.internal.sandbox.egress-proxy. Its
`start!` opens the proxy port for the session. Python execution sits in
com.blockether.vis.internal.python.runtime and the extension bridge in
com.blockether.vis.internal.python.extensions.

Tests use lazytest.core and clojure.string; shell steps use babashka.process.
The policy must stay strict: start the jail before you run any user code.

name: docs-tour.md
text:
# Manual tour

New readers start with the README.md and then Running a gateway. The concept pages
council.md, drafts.md, sessions.md and live-views.md explain each feature; the matching
API pages are council-api.md, drafts-api.md and sessions-api.md.

When something breaks, follow Reporting a bug. Automations have their own pages:
automations.md for the concept and automations-api.md for the calls.

Each page has a When to use section and a See also list. Before you start, read the
CHANGELOG.md entry for your version.

name: sdk-sessions.md
text:
## Reading sessions from the Python SDK

The SDK module packages/vis-agent/src/blockether/vis/_outside.py exposes
`list_sessions()` and `read_session()` for scripts outside the sandbox. Inside an
extension, use the `Sessions` class of blockether.vis.extension instead
(packages/vis-agent/src/blockether/vis/extension.py).

The TUI keeps its own transport: apps/vis-tui/src/com/blockether/vis/tui/client.clj
calls com.blockether.vis.tui.client/request! for each poll. The Council namespace
com.blockether.vis.internal.council.core has a `request!` of its own for peer questions.

A client should read the status, restore the cursor and run the request again.

name: pl-mixed.md
text:
## Synchronizacja sesji w aplikacji Companion

Aplikacja mobilna subskrybuje zmiany przez `SessionSubscriptionHub`. Ekran ustawień maszyny to `MachineSettings()`.
Klient gatewaya w Pythonie, czyli GatewayClient z modułu `engine/_client.py`, odpytuje sesje.
Gdy agent kończy turę, funkcja `read_session()` z pliku `vis/_outside.py` czyta historię sesji.

Szkice opisuje strona Drafts. Automatyzacje (Automations) uruchamiają prompt według harmonogramu.
Sesja, klient, żądanie i status to tutaj zwykłe słowa. Zażółć gęślą jaźń: Agent działa, Session trwa.
Funkcja `fold_session()` nie istnieje w grafie.

name: short-names.md
text:
# Running the agent

Call `run()` to start the job, then `get()` the result. The Session object holds state, and a Client sends each request.
To get the status, run the command again. A session can restore its client after a restart.

In `packages/vis-agent/src/blockether/vis/engine/_client.py` the `Session` class wraps the `GatewayClient`.
The `Agent` class in `engine/_agent.py` drives the loop and calls `run()` on every turn.

Settings live in the config. The main loop is simple. Get it, run it, request it.
